title: Applied ML Eval Integration Playbook (Eval harness, prompt sets, model onboarding, guardrails, quantization, regression)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines the integrated Applied ML evaluation lifecycle used at Redwood Inference. It consolidates guidance for the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage processes. The goal is to create a repeatable, auditable flow that balances output quality, cost, and performance for production inference.

Scope:
- Owned by Applied ML and Evals (engineering).
- Applies to all models targeted for Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers onboarding -> continuous evaluation -> regression detection -> triage/remediation.

Principles:
- Reproducibility: all evals must be runnable from the eval harness with pinned seed and environment.
- Signal-first: detect user-impacting regressions (quality, latency, cost) before rollout.
- Small-batch rollouts: gate model rollouts on eval and canary metrics.
- Instrumentation: every model and prompt-set must emit standardized metrics (latency P50/P95, cost-per-token, pass-rate).

Ownership and Roles

- Applied ML & Evals (owner): maintains eval-harness, benchmark corpus, regression triage playbooks, and quantization profiles.
- Model owner (team): provides prompt sets, runtime expectations, and business-specific evals.
- SRE/Platform: enforces SLOs for latency and availability, provides CI/CD integration.
- Product/Customer Success: defines acceptance criteria for customer-facing behavior.

High-level workflow

1. Model proposal + onboarding checklist submitted by model owner.
2. Eval harness onboarding run: core validation (smoke tests, safety checks, base metrics).
3. Generate baseline metrics + store artifact (baseline artifact includes prompts, responses, model config).
4. Define guardrails and thresholds.
5. Canary rollout with continuous evals and alerting.
6. Full rollout contingent on no regressions and SLO compliance.

Eval Harness (core)

Components:
- Runner: executes prompt sets across model variants, handles batching and repeatability.
- Data store: stores inputs, outputs, logs, and metric timeseries (linked to model-version).
- Scoring modules: accuracy/scoring, semantic similarity, hallucination detectors, safety classifiers.
- CI hooks: pre-merge checks and post-deploy continuous evaluation agents.

Minimum harness artifacts for every model-version:
- canonical_prompt_set.json (seeded examples),
- run_config.yaml (batch size, beam/search settings, sampling seeds),
- baseline_metrics.json (latency, cost, evaluation scores),
- eval_report.html (human-readable summary).

Example run_config.yaml:
```
# run_config.yaml
batch_size: 8
max_tokens: 512
temperature: 0.0
seed: 42
metrics: ["accuracy", "rouge", "semantic-similarity", "safety-score"]
```

Prompt sets and benchmarks

Guidelines for creating prompt sets:
- Representativeness: include 100	6,000 examples depending on scope (100 for narrow feature, 5k for broad benchmarks).
- Diversity: cover expected input lengths, languages, and edge-case formats.
- Labeling: each example must include ground-truth where applicable and a difficulty tag (easy/medium/hard).
- Versioned: use semantic versioning for prompt sets (e.g., v1.2.0).

Minimum prompt-set metadata table:

Name | Purpose | Size | Owner | Version | Tags
--- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---
customer-support-clarification | Measure clarification quality | 500 | support-ml | v1.0.0 | support,clarification
code-completion-smoke | Quick perf check for code models | 200 | devexp | v0.3.1 | code,perf

Benchmarking recommendations:
- Use fixed seeds and environment for perf comparisons.
- Run at realistic batch sizes observed in production.
- Produce both micro (unit) and macro (system-level) benchmarks.

Model onboarding checklist (mandatory)

1. Confirm model license and redistribution constraints.
2. Run eval-harness smoke run (sanity checks pass).
3. Generate baseline_metrics.json and upload to model registry.
4. Define guardrail thresholds (see section below).
5. Create canary plan (traffic %, duration, rollback criteria).
6. Provide quantization profile candidates if applicable.
7. Add to continuous eval pipeline.

Quality guardrails and thresholds

Standard signals and example thresholds (adjust per product):
- Latency P95 <= 250ms for interactive routes (critical).
- Token cost delta vs baseline <= +15%.
- Safety classifier pass-rate >= 99.5%.
- Semantic similarity (task-specific) >= 0.78 (or task-defined metric).
- Regression alert when any primary metric drops >5% relative to baseline and persists >30 minutes.

Guardrail configuration table (example)

Signal | Severity | Alert trigger | Owner
--- | --- | --- | ---
latency.P95 | critical | P95 > 250ms for 5m | SRE
cost.per_token | warning | delta > +20% vs baseline for 1h | Finance
safety.pass_rate | critical | < 99.5% for 10m | Security
semantic-similarity | warning | delta < -0.05 vs baseline for 30m | Applied ML

Quantization profiles (guidance)

Strategy summary:
- Prefer int8 quantization profiles validated by eval-harness for throughput-sensitive routes.
- Use mixed-precision only when supported by runtime and when quality loss < 1% on task metrics.
- Maintain a small set of vetted profiles per model (e.g., fp16, int8-ops, int8-kv-cache).

Sample quantization profile fields (to be stored in registry):
- profile_name, model_arch, quant_backend, accuracy_impact_estimate, recommended_routes, notes

Example quantization_profile.json (artifact)
```
{
  "profile_name": "gptx-13b-int8-default",
  "model_arch": "gptx-13b",
  "quant_backend": "onnxruntime-int8",
  "accuracy_impact_estimate": "0.8% average on NLU suite",
  "recommended_routes": ["non-critical-batch", "background-embedding"],
  "notes": "KV-cache quantization enabled; disable for long-context chat where quality is critical."
}
```

Regression detection and triage playbook

Detection:
- Continuous eval jobs run every 5	615 minutes for active canaries and hourly for production models.
- Primary metrics monitored: task score, semantic similarity, safety pass-rate, latency, error-rate, cost per token.
- Alerting: PagerDuty for critical severity; Slack channel for warnings with automated triage thread.

Automated triage steps (run by on-call Applied ML engineer):
1. Confirm alert and identify model-version and recent deployments.
2. Pull recent eval-harness run artifacts and compare to baseline artifact.
3. Run focused unit tests: seed the failing prompt-set subset and replicate the issue.
4. If reproducing: check changelog (model weights, tokenizer, quantization, runtime flags).
5. If not reproducing in harness: capture production traces and sample inputs; escalate to SRE for infra-induced regressions.
6. Determine remediation: rollback, config tweak (temperature, decoding), or model fix.
7. If rollback: execute canary rollback runbook (see below).
8. After fix: run full regression suite and rebaseline before re-rollout.

Prioritization matrix:
- Sev-1: Safety regressions or critical customer-impacting throughput/latency. Immediate rollback and incident.
- Sev-2: Task accuracy drop >10% or cost spike >50%\u2014fast mitigation within 4 hours.
- Sev-3: Minor metric drift or non-customer-facing degradations\u2014monitor and schedule fix within sprint.

Rollback and mitigation runbook (canary rollback example)

1. Pause traffic to canary (set routing weight to 0%).
2. Promote previous stable model-version for canary group.
3. Monitor primary metrics for 30 minutes.
4. If stable, re-run any outstanding customer-facing jobs and communicate to stakeholders.
5. Open a postmortem and schedule permanent remediation.

CI/CD integration and gates

- Pre-merge: unit-level evals must pass smoke tests in eval-harness.
- Pre-deploy: baseline metrics must be uploaded and compared; threshold gates must be green.
- Post-deploy (canary): continuous eval runs must show no regressions for policy window (default 24h) before full rollout.

Slack/PD alerting templates (example)

Slack: \"[ALERT] Model model-id vX.Y triggered safety-pass < 99.5% (current: 98.3%). Eval run: https://eval-runs/redwood/1234. Owner: @asha\"

Appendix: example checklist for a new model onboarding (one-page)

- [ ] License & export compliance verified
- [ ] Baseline eval-harness run completed
- [ ] Prompt sets added (canonical + product-specific)
- [ ] Guardrail thresholds entered in registry
- [ ] Quantization profile candidates uploaded
- [ ] Canary plan created in rollout tool
- [ ] Alerts and SLOs configured
